module_title: Advanced Analysis - Base Year, Nominal vs. Real GDP, and National Income
introduction: This is the most advanced level where we explore how inflation distorts economic data and learn the exact mathematical formula that the Government of India officially recognizes as the country's 'National Income'.

core_concepts.title: Market Price (MP) vs. Factor Cost (FC)
core_concepts.description: 1. Factor Cost (FC): The actual cost incurred inside the factory to produce a good (Land, Labor, Capital, Entrepreneurship). 2. Market Price (MP): The price at which the product is actually sold to the consumer. (Formula: MP = FC + Indirect Taxes - Subsidies).

core_concepts.title: The Official 'National Income' (NI)
core_concepts.description: Technically and officially, 'NNP at Factor Cost' (Net National Product at Factor Cost) is what economists formally call the 'National Income' of India. Formula: National Income (NNP_FC) = NNP_MP - Indirect Taxes + Subsidies.

core_concepts.title: Nominal GDP (Current Prices)
core_concepts.description: When GDP is calculated using the current year's market prices, it is called Nominal GDP. This metric is highly misleading because if a country produces the exact same number of goods as last year, but inflation causes prices to double, the Nominal GDP will artificially look like it doubled.

core_concepts.title: Real GDP (Constant Prices)
core_concepts.description: To find actual economic growth, economists calculate GDP using the prices of a fixed, constant 'Base Year' (currently 2011-12 in India). By locking the prices to a past year, Real GDP completely removes the illusion of inflation. It only grows if 'actual physical production' increases.

important_entities.name: GDP Deflator
important_entities.significance: The GDP Deflator measures the changes in prices for all the goods and services produced in an economy. (Formula: [Nominal GDP ÷ Real GDP] × 100). It is a much broader and more accurate measure of inflation than the CPI (Consumer Price Index) because it includes everything produced, not just a consumer basket.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Multiple Choice Questions often ask: 'Which of the following represents National Income?' Options: a) NNP at MP, b) NNP at FC, c) GDP at FC. Always choose 'NNP at FC'. Indirect taxes are government revenue, not the income earned by the 'factors of production' (citizens) of the nation.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Factory to Market: Add Taxes, Drop Subsidies
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: When a product leaves the Factory (FC) and goes to the Market (MP), the government slaps on an Indirect Tax (Add) and gives discounts/subsidies (Subtract).

exam_strategy_tips: UPSC frequently tests the conceptual difference between Real and Nominal GDP. Remember: 'Real GDP' is the only true indicator of economic growth and the standard of living, as Nominal GDP is heavily distorted by inflation.
